title: EXP-029 — Button Component Recovery Across Verified Coupled Unload
objective: On one new User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form `FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`, create exactly one native Toolbox Button, assign only Name=`FX_ButtonUnload01`, record its exact visible property-grid Type label, perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save, close the target Form exactly once, verify the existing `Unload IDO Metadata With Forms` preference remains enabled without changing it, invoke `Form > Definition > Unload All Global Form Objects` exactly once, then reopen the target exactly once through the same Designer's Form-menu recent-forms entry. Verify the same scoped Form recovers `FX_ButtonUnload01` with the identical Type label. Treat the result only as UI-level recovery of this Button definition across the tested coupled-unload workflow; do not claim database durability, backend identity, Caption persistence, IDO-metadata semantics, or behavior of other component properties/types.

acceptance_checks.description: Before mutation, evidence records the fresh worker/session identity, proves a usable live workflow in User scope while preserving inherited state untouched, shows a working known-existing Select Form positive control with Case Sensitive unchecked, and proves zero case-insensitive Name matches for `FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`. If a target match exists, stop blocked without altering it.

Evidence proves exactly one User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form `FX_ComponentUnloadLab01` was created through the fresh-dialog Classic/BuildFromScratch procedure with Save Template visibly unchecked, and the loaded Form identity is Name=`FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`, ScopeType=User, ScopeName=<current user>.
Before component placement, inspected evidence proves the target Form is clean and untouched and records the rendered canvas/component state without claiming complete component cardinality.

Exactly one native Toolbox Button creation operation is evidenced; only Name is assigned to `FX_ButtonUnload01`; authoritative property-grid/accessibility evidence records exact Name and the exact visible Type label before Save, with no unrelated component-property mutation.
Exactly one ordinary Designer Save is evidenced; afterward the target is clean and the component still reports exact Name=`FX_ButtonUnload01` and the identical Type label recorded in AC-4.

Exactly one ordinary target Form-tab close is evidenced; the target tab is gone, no unsaved-change or unexpected prompt appears, and the same Designer remains active. After close, the supported visible User Preferences surface shows `Unload IDO Metadata With Forms` enabled; it is left unchanged and preferences close without Save.

Exactly one `Form > Definition > Unload All Global Form Objects` invocation is evidenced after the target is closed. Post-action evidence shows no error/unexpected prompt, the target remains closed, the same Designer remains active, and no second unload or preference mutation occurred.

Exactly one reopen through the same Designer's Form-menu recent-forms entry is evidenced; the reopened Form has Name=`FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`, ScopeType=User, matching ScopeName, clean state, recovered component Name=`FX_ButtonUnload01`, and Type exactly equal to AC-4. If recent-forms is unavailable or session establishment is required after mutation, stop blocked.

Final read-only audit shows exactly one case-insensitive Select Form Name match for `FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`, re-confirms `Unload IDO Metadata With Forms` remains enabled and unchanged, reconciles exactly one Form creation, one Button creation, one Name assignment, one ordinary Save, one target close, one global-Form-object unload, and one recent-forms reopen, and proves experiment-authored repository changes are confined to the EXP-029 record and `evidence/EXP-029/`. The resulting finding is classified observed only; replay verification requires a later independent replay.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261007-182351-hVYe. Rationale: EXP-028 was blocked before any target mutation, so the next experiment should not work around its Button-Caption preflight issue. A distinct and well-grounded next capability is to extend the accepted EXP-027 Button-component recovery observation to the stronger, already replay-verified Form/global-object unload boundary used by EXP-006-R2 and EXP-007-R2. This keeps the component mutation minimal—one native Button and one Name assignment only—and asks one new question: whether the saved User-scoped Button definition, identified by Name plus its exact visible Type label, is recovered after an ordinary close followed by exactly one documented global-Form-object unload and same-Designer recent-forms reopen. It does not test Caption or any other component property.
